note: Day, night and weather (roadmap item 51; core/game/game_day.gd, checked by tools/check_data.gd). The world clock (item 27) already turns real seconds into years, seasons and a weather that is rolled each span; this adds the day. `GameDynasty.world_seconds` counts the seconds the clock has run (it holds still when the clock does), and a day is `day_seconds` of them, an abstract rhythm for the open world that is not tied to the length of a year. The sun's height over the day is -cos(2*pi*phase) (phase 0 is midnight, 0.5 noon); the light is how far it is above the horizon, ramping from dark to full across `twilight` either side of it, so a day has a night, a dawn, a day and a dusk. A day starts at `start_phase`. Night is when the sun's light is under `night_below` (it is the flag item 47's spawn tables and item 48's behaviour already take). The weather is the one the world already has (`world.weather_id`, rolled with the year); `weather_look` says what each does to the look of the world (how much of the light gets through, fog, rain or snow) and to how far a creature can see (`sight`), and fog and storms hide things in the open world. Colours are 0 to 1 red, green, blue. Nothing here is random or saved but the seconds, and the autopilot never feeds the clock.
